US-119-S675.description: A bill to contribute funds and artifacts to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota.
US-119-S675.aiSummary: The bill would let the Interior Secretary give up to $50 million in grants to help build the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota, but only after the project has at least $100 million from state or other non-federal money. The money could be used to preserve Roosevelt-related materials and to provide public education, but not to run or maintain the library. It would also allow federal agencies to loan museum items and other artifacts to the foundation for the library, and says the federal government would not run the library.

US-119-HR10891.title: Scams Tax Relief Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10891.description: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to remove the limitation on deductions for theft losses involving fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation and to allow such deductions without regard to whether the taxpayer itemizes other deductions.
US-119-HR10891.aiSummary: The bill would change tax rules so people who lose money to theft tied to fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation could deduct those losses. It would also let them take that deduction even if they do not itemize other deductions. The change would apply to losses after the date the bill becomes law.

US-119-HR10792.title: FTC Whistleblower Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

US-119-HR10792.description: To provide incentives for and protect whistleblowers under the authority of the Federal Trade Commission, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10792.aiSummary: The bill would add new protections for people who report possible violations tied to the Federal Trade Commission. It would bar retaliation against whistleblowers, block some gag rules and arbitration deals from being enforced against them, and let some whistleblowers sue for reinstatement, back pay, and other damages. It would also create a reward program that could pay whistleblowers a share of money collected in covered FTC cases.

US-119-HR10770.title: 340B Rebate Model Delay Act
US-119-HR10770.summary:
340B Rebate Model Delay Act

This bill temporarily limits the use of rebates for prescription drugs under the 340B program and delays the implementation of the 340B Rebate Model Pilot Program.

Under current law, the 340B program generally limits the maximum price drug manufacturers participating in Medicaid or Medicare can charge eligible health care organizations for covered outpatient drugs. Beginning on January 1, 2027, and ending on December 31, 2028, the bill prohibits drug manufacturers from entering agreements with 340B organizations that require the organization to pay more than the allowable ceiling price for a covered outpatient drug at the time of purchase and subsequently receive a rebate to comply with the maximum price requirements.

The bill also delays until January 1, 2029, the implementation of the 340B Rebate Model Pilot Program. The pilot program allows approved drug manufacturers to charge 340B organizations full price for certain high-impact drugs and provide a rebate that reduces the amount paid to the allowable ceiling price after the drug is dispensed. Under the pilot program, the rebates are verified and issued on a claim-by-claim basis.
US-119-HR10770.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2026-10-09)

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10770.aiSummary: The bill would limit some rebate deals for prescription drugs in the 340B program from January 1, 2027, through December 31, 2028. It would stop drug makers from using agreements that make covered health care groups pay more than the allowed price first and then get a rebate later. It would also delay the 340B Rebate Model Pilot Program until January 1, 2029.

US-119-HR10352.title: 504 Program Level Flexibility Act
US-119-HR10352.summary:
504 Program Level Flexibility Act

This bill authorizes the Small Business Administration (SBA), upon a determination that the amount of its commitments to guarantee loans under the 504 Loan Program could exceed the authorized annual limit, to guarantee up to 115% of that limit.

The 504 Loan Program provides a small business with SBA financing—through a certified development company intermediary—for expansion or modernization.

The bill requires the SBA to notify Congress if it intends to use this authority. The SBA may exercise the authority only once each fiscal year.

US-119-HR10671.title: Securing Our Critical Infrastructure Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10671.description: To amend the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022 to reauthorize a program of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency relating to security vulnerability warnings, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10671.aiSummary: The bill would reauthorize a Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency program that sends security warning notices about weak spots in computer systems. It would apply to covered utilities, including some water and wastewater utilities and certain public water and treatment works operators. It would also add rules for sharing and protecting private information, automatic cyber hygiene services, and help with incident response, and the program would end five years after that section takes effect.

US-119-HR10594.title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10594.description: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to carry out prize competitions to advance the science of interpretability and to develop adversarial robustness with respect to artificial intelligence products, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10594.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to run at least one prize contest to improve how people understand artificial intelligence systems and at least one to make them more resistant to attacks. It would involve work with other federal officials and experts, and it would cover AI products used in government or industry. The bill also authorizes $10 million for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 and would require a report to Congress after the first contest ends.

US-119-HR10495.title: CATFISH Act of 2026

US-119-HR10495.description: To amend title 18, United States Code, to establish enhanced penalties for certain frauds, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10495.aiSummary: The bill would add tougher criminal penalties for certain fraud tied to romance scams that target people age 60 or older. It would also require training for some financial institutions and retailers, including help for gift card purchases over $500, and new reporting steps when a senior customer shows signs of possible fraud. Covered financial institutions would have to report warning signs, keep records of these events, and set up procedures to help protect senior customers.

US-119-HR9385.description: To prohibit entities integral to the national interests of the United States from participating in any foreign sustainability due diligence regulation, including the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive of the European Union, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9385.aiSummary: The bill would bar certain U.S. businesses and other entities that are seen as tied to the national interests of the United States from following foreign sustainability due diligence rules, including the European Union’s corporate sustainability rule. US-119-HR6470.title: Increasing Baseline Updates Act
US-119-HR6470.summary:
Increasing Baseline Updates Act

This bill requires the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to submit to Congress at least two updates to its annual baseline unless CBO is otherwise directed by the chairs of the congressional budget committees. At least one of the updates must include the economic data used by CBO to calculate the update.

(A baseline is a projection of federal spending and receipts during a fiscal year under current law. Under current law, CBO is required to publish the baseline by February 15 of each year. While there is no statutory requirement for specific updates, CBO generally provides an update with its analysis of the President's annual budget request. It has also provided some updates during the summer, depending on the timing of the President's budget request.)

The bill also requires the President to submit technical budget data to Congress on or before February 1 of each year to the extent this is practicable. Currently, federal agencies provide the data to Congress as part of the President's budget request.
US-119-HR6470.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-12-04)

US-119-HR10473.title: Justice for Ukrainian Children Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10473.description: To authorize amounts for the purpose of investigating, documenting, verifying, and preventing the Russian Federation's ongoing and systemic unlawful transfer, deportation, indoctrination, and militarization of Ukrainian children, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10473.aiSummary: The bill would provide at least $15 million a year from fiscal years 2027 through 2032 to help gather evidence, track, rescue, and help children from Ukraine who were taken to Russia. It would also require sanctions on foreign people the President finds helped with the transfer, deportation, indoctrination, or militarization of these children, and it would bar them from U.S. entry and freeze certain property. In addition, it would authorize at least $10 million a year for Ukraine- and nearby region-language broadcasts by Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty and Voice of America, and it would require reports to Congress from the Secretary of State and the U.S. Agency for Global Media.

US-119-HR10374.title: Affordable Premiums for Seniors Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10374.description: To require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to continue the Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration under the Medicare program.
US-119-HR10374.aiSummary: The bill would require the Health and Human Services Secretary to keep the Medicare Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration going for 2027 through 2029 in a way like 2026. It would also keep it going in 2030 and later years unless the Secretary finds ending it would not raise premiums for people in Medicare Part D prescription drug plans. The Secretary would have to issue updated rules for how the program works for 2027 within 30 days after the bill becomes law.

US-119-HR10330.title: Higher Education Oversight for Nonprofits Ensuring Standards and Transparency Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10330.description: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose restrictions on university tax inquiries and examinations, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10330.aiSummary: The bill would add new rules for IRS tax inquiries and exams of universities. It would require a high-level Treasury official to have a written reason before an inquiry starts, require written notice to the school, and give the school a chance for a conference before an exam. It would also set time limits, add approval steps before some tax changes or assessments, and limit repeated inquiries for the same school.

US-119-HR10275.title: Puerto Rico Energy Opportunity and Geothermal Assessment Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10275.description: To amend the Energy Policy Act of 1992 to require the Secretary of the Interior to conduct certain geothermal assessments for the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
US-119-HR10275.aiSummary: The bill would require the Interior Department, through the U.S. Geological Survey, to conduct geothermal studies for Puerto Rico. The work would include high-detail maps, checks on groundwater risk, and checks on earthquake risks tied to enhanced geothermal systems. It would also require reports to House and Senate committees within 1 year after enactment and every 2 years after that until the study is done.

US-119-HR10176.title: No PRC Seafood in Congress Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10176.description: To prohibit Chinese seafood products in congressional dining facilities, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10176.aiSummary: The bill would bar seafood products from China from being bought, served, or sold in dining spots in the Capitol and other congressional dining facilities. It would also require the offices that run those facilities to set rules within 180 days if the bill became law. Suppliers would have to name every country where the seafood was caught, raised, made, or processed and keep records to back that up.

US-119-HR9561.title: Shandra Eisenga TB Study Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9561.description: To direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to conduct a study on the feasibility of developing an accurate and reliable standardized test for detecting tuberculosis in tissue from a human cadaver, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9561.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Health and Human Services Secretary to study whether a standard test can be made to detect tuberculosis in tissue from a human body after death. The study would look at donor screening, transplant safety, and other issues tied to organ and tissue donation. The secretary would also have to report the findings to Congress, and the work would involve health agencies and groups that handle organ and tissue donations.

US-119-S356.title: Secure Rural Schools Reauthorization Act of 2025
US-119-S356.summary:
Secure Rural Schools Reauthorization Act of 2025

This act extends and modifies the Secure Rural Schools (SRS) program, under which states and counties containing certain federal land may receive payments from the Forest Service or the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) for schools, roads, and certain other municipal services.

The act modifies the SRS program, including by
• extending payments made to states and counties containing federal land through FY2026,
• providing lapsed payments for FY2024 and FY2025,
• extending the authority of counties to initiate projects using such funds through FY2028, and
• extending the authority to initiate projects proposed by resource advisory committees through FY2028.
